artists.name: Jin
artists.bio: I work in two registers. Fine line for the pieces that live quietly on skin, micro-realism for the ones that ask you to look twice. Precision isn't the goal — it's the floor.

artists.name: Jaya
artists.bio: Japanese traditional taught me patience. A sleeve isn't a drawing — it's a composition that has to move with the body for a lifetime. I design for how it will read in thirty years.

artists.name: Sini
artists.bio: New school is where colour stops apologizing. Bold lines, saturated palettes, characters with attitude. If you want a piece people ask about, we'll get along.

artists.name: Hanu
artists.bio: I held a brush long before I held a machine. The pressure, the release, the single stroke that can't be redone — that discipline is what I bring to skin.

artists.name: Jay
artists.bio: Illustration first, tattoo second. Every piece starts as a drawing that would hold up on paper. Fine line is just how I move it onto skin without losing the hand.

artists.name: Tan
artists.bio: I run front of house. I greet everyone who walks in, supervise every session from the nearest warm spot, and I have never once missed a snack. Ask for me by name.
